summary: Natalie Depraz is a philosopher who studied at ENS de Fontenay-Saint-Cloud and Paris Nanterre University. She held posts at the Collège international de philosophie, Paris-Sorbonne, University of Rouen Normandy, and Galatasaray University, and founded the Rouen School of Phenomenology.
Natalie Gummer works in Buddhist and religious studies. She held posts at Harvard University (attested 2001) and Beloit College, where she was appointed professor of religious studies in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Stephan V. Beyer, also studying under Ngawang Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Legden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
Natalie Rothman is a historian who completed her studies at the University of Michigan (1999–2006). In 2006, she took up a post at the University of Toronto.
Natasha Heller works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. After completing her PhD at Harvard University in 2005, she held posts at UC Berkeley (attested 2008) and UCLA (attested 2016).

Natasha Reichle works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, under Joanna Gottfried Williams, also studying with Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.
Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD under Hans T. Bakker at the University of Groningen between circa 2012 and 2018, while also holding a post there.

Nathan Sivin was a sinologist and historian of science. Educated at MIT and Harvard University, he taught at MIT (1966–1977) before serving as Professor of Chinese Culture and of the History of Science at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–2006).

Nathan W. Hill, a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology, studied at Harvard University. He was a reader at SOAS (circa 2008–2019) and became Sam Lam Professor in Chinese Studies at Trinity College Dublin in 2021.
Nathaniel Brassey Halhed worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at Harrow School and Christ Church, he served as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.
Nathaniel DeWitt Garson works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, having also studied under Khenpo Namdrol.
Nathaniel Wallich studied at the University of Copenhagen (circa 1801–1806) and later served as Superintendent of the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden from circa 1817 to 1846.

Nathmal Tatia was an Indologist and philosopher who earned a Doctor of Literature at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee and studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (attested 1982–1990).
Navina Lamminger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard.
Nawang Tsering Shakspo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Lal Mani Joshi and served as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1985).
Neal Donner works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of British Columbia, where he was taught by Leon Hurvitz (attested 1976).

Nenghai Shi was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Peking University and under teachers including Kecheng Zhang and Khangsar Rinpoche. He founded the Shaocheng Society and served as vice-president of the Buddhist Association of China (1953–1966).
Newton Mohun Dutt worked in Indology and served as Curator of Libraries for Baroda State, the Central Library of Baroda, and the Baroda State Department of Archaeology from circa 1922 to 1933.
Ng-Fung Yuen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of the West under the supervision of Kottegoda Warnasuriya (attested 2009).
Ngak Sé Rigpé Dorjé studied under Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok and Khenpo Tsultrim Lodro.
